title: GET https://ar-gcp-cdn.bistudio.com/manifest/<2 hex>/<2 hex>/<sha512>/<size>
$comment: Observed on 1.8.0.13 while downloading one Workshop addon: one 200 per file, 120-2747 bytes, three files. The path is the manifestPath that assets/download-list returned, and the answer says which fragments make up the file - the fragmented download protocol the binary calls the Fragmentizer. The fragments themselves are fetched from /fragment/<2 hex>/<2 hex>/<sha512>/<size> on the same host, one per fragment (about twenty for a 16 KB addon), and those answers are binary unless the fragment happens to be a JSON file of the addon: in the capture one fragment parsed as the mod's own config, {baseRestUrl, authToken, extensions:[...]}, and another as the addon.gproj content. This schema describes the manifest only; the fragment endpoint returns raw bytes and is not a JSON API.

size.description: The size of the whole file; it matches the `size` of the same file in assets/download-list, and the final path segment of the manifest URL.

sha512.description: SHA-512 of the whole file, 128 hex characters - the same value that appears in the URL path.

remainder.description: The tail of the file when it does not divide evenly into fragments, null when it does (the 2079-byte and 120-byte files in the capture have null).

offsets.description: One entry per fragment that carries data for this remainder; -1 for a fragment that is a duplicate of another, as in the captured 14-fragment manifest.

sha512.description: The fragment's own hash - fetch /fragment/<2>/<2>/<sha512>/<size> with exactly this value and size.

offsets.description: Where in the file this fragment's bytes go: one offset per occurrence, 0 for the first fragment of a simple file, -1 for a duplicate reference. The captured 14-fragment manifest for a 14431-byte data.pak uses 56 for the first fragment and has a remainder of 886 bytes.
